newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's FIS wants doctors to visit jailed leaders.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's FIS wants doctors to visit jailed leaders.

text.p: Algeria's outlawed Moslem fundamentalist opposition group urged the Algerian government on Wednesday to allow independent doctors to visit its jailed leaders, and suggested one of them may have died in prison.

"The Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) calls (on the authorities) to permit a neutral medical team to check the health situation of its leadership, namely Ali Belhadj, to confirm whether he is still alive," the group's Washington-based leader, Anwar Haddam, said in a faxed statement.

Haddam said the authorities had thrown a cloak of secrecy over the state of jailed FIS leaders Abassi Madani, his deputy Belhadj and Abdelkader Hachani since last year, keeping their families and supporters in the dark about their health.

"The FIS calls on foreign states which advocate the defence of freedom, human rights and free speech to exert pressure on (President Liamine) Zeroual in order to end ambiguity over the situation of the FIS leaders," he added.

FIS president Madani and Belhadj were sentenced in 1991 to 12 years in jail for threatening Algeria's security. Hachani, who took over the leadership in 1991, has been held in prison without trial since January 1992 over a statement criticising army chiefs.
Zeroual allowed Madani and Belhadj out of jail and put them under house arrest in 1994 in a bid to end Algeria's civil strife through dialogue.
The two men were believed to have been sent back to prison after the dialogue failed in July 1995.

An estimated 50,000 people have died in Algeria's war between Islamist rebels and the military-backed government since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which the FIS, since outlawed, had taken a strong lead.
